text: Your slab looks dry and hard. That does not mean it is done.
Concrete does not get strong by drying. It gets strong by curing.
Inside, the cement reacts with water. That reaction builds strength, slowly, day by day.
If the water leaves too early, from sun or wind, the reaction slows down.
The surface can crack, and the concrete can end up weaker than it was designed to be.
So curing means keeping it wet and covered. Ponding on the slab. Wet sacks on columns. Spraying on walls.
How many days? That depends on the cement and the weather. Ask your engineer for the number, and write it down.
Then decide who waters it, every single day.
Save this before your slab day.
